chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sulaym al-Farra', from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'It is befitting for the believer that he not die until he learns the Quran, or is in the process of learning it.'

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِن: The believer (Mu'min) — one who has true faith; in the Shia tradition, often implies deeper commitment than mere Islam
key_terms.تَعْلِيمِهِ: Its learning/teaching — both the act of learning and being in the pedagogical process; the pronoun refers to the Quran
key_terms.يَنْبَغِي: It is befitting/it behoves — an expression of strong moral expectation without the absolute force of obligation (wujub), yet stronger than mere recommendation (mustahabb)

ai.seo_question: Does a Muslim need to learn the Quran before death according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) declares that every believer has a moral obligation to learn the Quran before death, or at minimum to be actively engaged in its study. This teaching was directed at the Shia community during a period when Quran memorization and recitation were central to religious identity. The phrase 'or be in its learning' offers a compassionate qualification — commitment to the learning process itself is sufficient, recognizing the difficulty some may face.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Suleym Al Fara’a, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is befitting for the Momin that he does not die until he learns the Quran, or happens to be in its learning (process)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sulaym al-Farra’ from a man from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
It is worthwhile for a Muslim to learn the Holy Quran before his death or should be in the process of learning.’”
